title: Tenant NOC Handoff and Safe-Mode Orchestration Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines the operational handoff between Redwood Field Engineering (FieldEng) and the Customer NOC for private VPC or on-prem tenants, and the procedures to put a tenant into Safe-Mode (degrader/fallback) during network or runtime emergencies. It codifies the preconditions, ownership, verification steps, and rollback/evidence capture so the handoff is auditable and repeatable.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: VPC and air-gapped on-prem private deployments where Redwood provides a managed control plane with on-prem runtime + customer NOC for network and first-line support.
- Audience: Field Engineering, Customer NOC, Redwood Oncall, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success.

Preconditions (must be satisfied before handoff)
------------------------------------------------
1. Control plane API and management endpoints reachable over agreed management path (IP allowlist validated).
2. Prometheus/Loki traces and metrics forwarding confirmed to Redwood telemetry endpoint or customer-observed mirror.
3. Keys and rotation process (KMS/HSM) validated: test encrypt/decrypt round-trip using the customer's KMS credentials.
4. Tenant runbook and emergency contact list uploaded to shared incident binder (S3/secure bucket).
5. NOC access checklist completed: VPN accounts issued, jumpbox approved, and `redwoodctl` role-bound to the NOC service account.

Ownership matrix
----------------
| Activity | Primary | Backup | Contact (pager/Slack) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Handoff coordination | FieldEng | Solutions Eng | fieldeng-oncall@redwood.com (pager: #fieldeng-rot) |
| Safe-Mode activation | Customer NOC | Redwood Oncall | noc-ops@customer.com / redwood-oncall@redwood.com |
| Telemetry verification | Redwood Observability | Customer NOC | observability@redwood.com |
| Rollback / model swap | Redwood Serving Runtime Team | FieldEng | runtime-oncall@redwood.com |

SLOs and thresholds to communicate to NOC
-----------------------------------------
- 99th percentile inference latency target: <= 150 ms (for pinned model small-seq workloads).
- Acceptable degraded latency in Safe-Mode: <= 500 ms (documented fallback variant).
- Error rate threshold that triggers Safe-Mode: 5% 5xx or 10% increase over baseline error rate sustained for 3 minutes.
- Telemetry heartbeat: control-plane heartbeat metric (control_plane.heartbeat) must be present every 60s. Missing > 3 intervals => escalate.

Handoff checklist (pre-handoff)
-------------------------------
- [ ] Confirm topology document (network CIDR, BGP peering, NAT/GW positions) delivered to NOC.
- [ ] Provide `redwoodctl` read-only and safemode roles; test credentials.
- [ ] Deploy synthetic-sourced metrics fixture: `synthetic/latency-smoke` and verify visibility.
- [ ] Agree escalation matrix and communication channels (primary Slack channel and 3 escalation emails/pagers).
- [ ] Provide a documented Safe-Mode policy JSON for the tenant (see example below).

Safe-Mode policy (example)
--------------------------
The Safe-Mode policy is a small JSON document the control plane uses to decide: which model variant to route to, traffic fraction, and timeouts. Example: 

```
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp-42",
  "trigger_conditions": {
    "5xx_error_rate_pct": 5,
    "latency_increase_pct": 100,
    "duration_seconds": 180
  },
  "fallback": {
    "model_variant": "gptx-medium-quant4",
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "streaming": false,
    "traffic_shift_percent": 100
  },
  "auto_recover": {
    "recheck_interval_seconds": 60,
    "min_healthy_intervals": 3
  }
}
```

Activation procedure (when threshold met)
-----------------------------------------
1. NOC observes threshold breach (alerts fire) and performs quick triage using metrics/dashboards.
2. If breach matches Safe-Mode trigger, NOC posts a status update to the agreed Slack channel and pages Redwood Oncall.
3. NOC runs the Safe-Mode preflight check: verify control_plane.heartbeat, confirm not a telemetry false-positive (run `redwoodctl metrics query control_plane.heartbeat --tenant acme-corp-42 --window 5m`).
4. NOC initiates Safe-Mode using the `redwoodctl` command (role-bound account):

```
redwoodctl tenant safemode activate --tenant acme-corp-42 --policy ./acme-safemode-policy.json --reason "latency spike 2026-06-15T14:12Z"
```

5. Control plane replies with an activation event; NOC validates routing by running a small synthetic request through the tenant ingress and confirming expected variant in response headers: `x-redwood-model: gptx-medium-quant4`.
6. NOC maintains Safe-Mode and monitors the auto_recover checks; if metrics stabilize (min_healthy_intervals satisfied), the control plane will auto-roll back Safe-Mode. If auto rollback fails or wrong behavior observed, proceed to explicit rollback (next section).

Verification and post-activation validation
-------------------------------------------
- Verify 95th/99th latency improved vs pre-activation by at least 30% within 5 minutes.
- Confirm error rate drops to below threshold (<= 2%).
- Run 10 synthetic requests across typical payload sizes and confirm model shape and token output roughly match baseline (sanity check).
- Take and attach screenshots of dashboard panels (latency, errors, model-variant distribution) to the incident ticket.

Rollback and explicit deactivation
---------------------------------
When auto_recover does not restore service or wrong behavior observed:
1. Open incident and set owner to Runtime Team.
2. Runtime Team performs one of the following, in order:
   a. Partial traffic shift: `redwoodctl traffic shift --tenant acme-corp-42 --to model: gptx-base --percent 50` and monitor.
   b. Swap to previous pinned model version (transactional model swap): `redwoodctl model swap --tenant acme-corp-42 --from gptx-medium-quant4 --to gptx-medium-v1 --transactional true --preserve_kv true`
   c. If model swap is not viable, reinstate full traffic to a resiliency fallback (e.g., smaller context model) with explicit customer sign-off.
3. After rollback action, collect forensic evidence (see next section) and update incident timeline.

Forensic evidence capture (minimum)
----------------------------------
- Control Plane event export: `redwoodctl events export --tenant acme-corp-42 --since 2026-06-15T14:00Z --until 2026-06-15T15:30Z > events.json`
- KV cache snapshot (if applicable): `redwoodctl kv snapshot --tenant acme-corp-42 --output kv-snap.tar.gz`
- Logs: compressed Loki query result for the window.
- Telemetry export: Prometheus range query and Grafana panel snapshots.
- Attach all artifacts to the incident ticket and S3 evidence bucket; keep retention metadata.

Failure injection and validation (recommended quarterly)
-----------------------------------------------------
Purpose: verify NOC safe-mode activation, verify rollback and evidence capture.
Test types and expected outcomes:
- Control-plane partition simulation: block control-plane egress for 2 minutes; expected: NOC activates safemode and synthetic traffic is routed to fallback model; proof: header `x-redwood-fallback: true`.
- Latency spike simulation: inject 200–500ms additional latency to model-serving path; expected: safemode triggers and latency reduces by >= 30% post-activation.
- KV eviction test: force KV eviction on a single shard; expected: degraded QoS but absence of catastrophic errors; eviction metrics recorded.

Runbook snippets and commands
----------------------------
- Check heartbeat: `redwoodctl metrics query control_plane.heartbeat --tenant <tenant> --window 5m`
- Activate safemode: `redwoodctl tenant safemode activate --tenant <tenant> --policy <policy.json>`
- Deactivate safemode: `redwoodctl tenant safemode deactivate --tenant <tenant> --reason "resolved"`
- Export events: `redwoodctl events export --tenant <tenant> --since <ISO> --until <ISO> > events.json`
- Traffic shift: `redwoodctl traffic shift --tenant <tenant> --to model:<model-name> --percent <int>`

Observability contract to hand to NOC
-------------------------------------
- Required metrics (every 60s): control_plane.heartbeat, tenant.request.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, tenant.request.errors.5xx, tenant.kv.evictions, tenant.model.variant_distribution.
- Required logs: ingress request logs, model-run logs with request_id, and model-variant headers.
- Traces: sample request traces must include control-plane decisions and model-runtime spans.

Communication templates
-----------------------
Slack incident kickoff (NOC -> Redwood):
```
INCIDENT: acme-corp-42 latency spike 2026-06-15T14:12Z
Summary: p99 latency rising to 1.2s, 5xx rate 8%.
Action: Activating tenant Safe-Mode (gptx-medium-quant4) per agreed policy. Paging runtime-oncall@redwood.com
Evidence: dashboards attached.
```

Email to customer (after stabilization):
```
Subject: [Acme Corp] Resolved: Tenant Safe-Mode activation
Body: We observed a latency spike at 2026-06-15T14:12Z and activated Safe-Mode to restore availability. We have captured forensic artifacts and will follow up with a full RCA within 48 hours.
```

Post-incident RCA expectations
------------------------------
- FieldEng + Runtime Team produce a post-incident report within 72 hours. Include timeline, root cause hypothesis, code/config change if any, and suggested mitigation (e.g., model quantization fallback adjustments, autoscaling tuning, or priority KV shard pinning).
- Customer Success reviews and proposes follow-up items with the customer.

Appendices
---------
A. Safe-Mode JSON schema (link to schema page)
B. `redwoodctl` permissions matrix and example RBAC policy (YAML snippet)
C. Evidence retention policy and S3 path template: `s3://redwood-evidence/private-deploys/<tenant_id>/<incident-ts>/`
